name: Threads (Meta)

field_reviews.reason: Official get-started doc confirms Threads user access tokens 'conform to the OAuth 2.0 protocol' with an Authorization Window issuing authorization codes exchanged for user access tokens.
OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow issues short/long-lived user access tokens that are sent as bearer tokens on API requests; both entries are accurate.

Confirmed live at developers.facebook.com/docs/threads/get-started/: creating a Meta app with the Threads use case is self-serve and 'Threads testers can grant your app these permissions at any time', but for non-tester users 'each permission must first be approved through the App Review process, and your app must be published'. Production approval status re-checked as instructed: per-permission App Review (screencast of the full user journey) plus app publication is required; third-party integrators also report Meta Tech Provider Verification as a prerequisite for advanced access.

Permission list (threads_basic, content_publish, delete, keyword_search, manage_insights, manage_mentions, manage_replies, profile_discovery, read_replies) confirms a publishing/replies/insights-focused API with no ads or DMs - medium is fair.
Threads API is a REST-style Graph API at graph.threads.net; no GraphQL or MCP endpoint documented.
Independently confirmed: no official Meta MCP for Threads found, and the live Composio catalog (1183 toolkits, grepped for 'threads') contains no Threads toolkit.
Development against your own account and designated testers works immediately after self-serve app creation; the full API surface is exercisable pre-review.
Per-permission Meta App Review with screencast (community sources report 2-4 weeks per permission) plus app publication gates production use for arbitrary users - correct blocker.

notes: Re-checked app-review/production-approval status as instructed: official docs confirm self-serve dev access via testers and per-permission App Review plus published-app requirement for ordinary users. Draft evidence URL developers.facebook.com/docs/threads/get-started/ confirmed live with the exact quoted language. No Threads MCP in Composio catalog or from Meta.
